bns:Component.name: Consume_P2P_ExecutionLog_Event
bns:Component.bns:description: Event Streams Consume operation for Sub_TransactionLog_Consumer, replacing Listen_P2P_ExecutionLog_Event. RENAMED 2026-09-28: topic is now "edv.transaction.log" (was "esb.p2p.transaction.log" - consolidated onto the pre-existing edv.* naming convention), subscription "p2p-transaction-log-consumer" recreated fresh on the new topic (the old subscription of the same name on the old topic, and several throwaway test subscriptions, were left behind - not deleted). SEPARATELY: the original topic name had a typo bug for months ("esb.transaction.log", missing ".p2p.") that made this Consume read from an empty topic no matter what - fixed same day, before this rename. Consume can read an existing subscription regardless of which operation type created it. Chosen because Listen requires an execution worker enabled on the cloud runtime, which was confirmed absent (subscription "type" stays "NONE" no matter how many times the Listen process is deployed/triggered - see platform_entities/event_streams.md). Consume is an ordinary on-demand execution needing no worker, at the cost of needing an external trigger (schedule) rather than reacting to messages instantly. UNRELIABLE IN TESTING 2026-09-28: repeated Consume calls against a subscription with a confirmed non-zero backlog (verified via GraphQL backlogCount) returned "0 documents found" most of the time (5 of 8 attempts docs found), tried across Shared and Exclusive subscriptionType and fresh subscriptions - cause not isolated, may be a platform-side timing/consistency issue. A scheduled, recurring Consume should eventually drain a message via redelivery, but visibility latency is not reliably bounded by the schedule interval alone - flagged for the user, not resolved. acknowledgeLater=true: the message is only acked after the process succeeds; on failure it returns to the backlog for redelivery on a platform-determined ~1-2 minute interval (not configurable via acknowledgementTimeout) - reasonable here since the downstream action is an idempotent UPDATE keyed on transaction_id, so redelivery/reprocessing is harmless. maxMessages=10 per poll is a starting point, not a measured value - tune based on real event volume once scheduled. | built with boomi-companion v1.0.57
